content: If a woman in labor is not in active labor (cervix dilated 0-3 cm with weak contractions occurring less than twice in 10 minutes), the following steps should be taken: 1. Monitoring and Assessment: Check for emergency signs every hour using rapid assessment methods. Monitor the frequency, intensity, and duration of contractions. Assess fetal heart rate and cervical dilation every four hours unless otherwise indicated. Avoid performing vaginal examinations more frequently than every four hours unless necessary. Record all findings in the labor record and partograph, including the time of membrane rupture and the color of the amniotic fluid. 2. Supportive Care: Refer the woman urgently to a hospital if needed. If the woman is discharged, advise her to return if pain or discomfort increases, vaginal bleeding occurs, or the membranes rupture. When the woman enters active labor (cervix dilated 4 cm or more), the following steps should be taken: 1. Frequent Monitoring: Check for emergency signs every 30 minutes. Monitor contractions, fetal heart rate, and cervical dilation. Avoid unnecessary vaginal examinations (limit to every four hours unless indicated). Record findings in the labor record and partograph. 2. Support and Comfort: Encourage the woman to empty her bladder and stay hydrated, but avoid solid foods. Support her in adopting an upright position or walking if she wishes. Reassess progress every two hours and refer if there is no progress. During the second stage of labor (cervix fully dilated, perineum bulging, and head visible): 1. Delivery Preparation: The delivery area should be clean and warm (25°C). Assist the woman into a comfortable, upright position of her choice and provide emotional and physical support. Do not allow the woman to lie flat on her back. 2. Delivery of the Baby: Allow the woman to push as she feels the urge during contractions. Do not urge her to push. If the perineum does not begin to thin and stretch after 30 minutes of pushing, perform a vaginal examination to confirm full cervical dilation. If the cervix is not fully dilated, discourage pushing and encourage breathing techniques. Wait until the head is visible and the perineum is distending before proceeding with delivery. 3. Immediate Newborn Care: Place the baby on the mother’s abdomen or in her arms immediately after delivery. Thoroughly dry the baby and assess breathing. If the baby is not breathing or gasping, initiate newborn resuscitation immediately. Keep the baby warm and encourage skin-to-skin contact with the mother. During the third stage of labor (delivery of the placenta): 1. Placenta Delivery: Administer 10 IU of oxytocin intramuscularly to the mother to aid uterine contraction. Use controlled cord traction to deliver the placenta while applying counter-traction to the uterus. If the placenta does not descend within 30-40 seconds, release traction and wait for the uterus to contract again before repeating the process. Examine the placenta and membranes for completeness. If incomplete, remove any retained fragments manually. 2. Postpartum Monitoring: If heavy bleeding occurs, massage the uterus to expel clots and administer additional oxytocin as needed. Refer urgently to a hospital if bleeding persists. 3. Care for the Mother and Baby: Keep the mother and baby together in the delivery room for at least one hour after delivery. Encourage breastfeeding and provide support as needed. If complications arise during labor or delivery, such as a prolapsed cord, breech presentation, or shoulder dystocia, take immediate action to manage the situation and refer to a hospital if necessary.
